title: Family, Neighbors, and Helpers
objectives: I can say who is in my family and who is my neighbor.
I can name a helper and a place in my community.
I can tell what I can do at the library.
rationale: These five words take children from home outward to the people and places they know. Family and neighbor are concrete and close; helper names a role; library is a place many children visit; and community is the big idea that holds the rest. Community is a Tier 3 word and is taught last, as a name for what children have already met. The unit revisits safe, share, together, and listen from the first unit by asking how people in a community treat each other.

passage.title: Ben at the Library

teacher.overview: Children learn five words about the people and places around them by drawing and talking about their own lives, then hear them in a short story about a family trip to the library. All activities are oral or drawn; no reading is needed.

notes.va.family.n: Families look many ways. Say 'the people who care for you at home' and let children name their own. Do not ask for a specific kind of family, and never require a mother and father.
notes.va.neighbor.n: A neighbor lives near you, such as next door or on your street. Children may call any friend a neighbor, so check that the person lives close. The related word neighborhood is not taught yet.
notes.va.community.n: Tier 3 word taught last. Start from what children know, such as school, park, and library, and say 'all of these are part of our community'. Draw a class community map together.
notes.va.helper.n: Helper is help plus -er, the person who does the helping. Ask children for helpers they know, and include class jobs such as paper helper. Avoid saying only adults can be helpers.
notes.va.library.n: Visit if you can. A library lends books for free and keeps a quiet space. Children may confuse library with bookstore, so say 'borrow and bring back'. Review quiet from the senses unit.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'I live with my family. My neighbor lives next door. Our community has a park, a school, and a library. At the library, the librarian is a helper. Let's draw our community and say each word.'
discuss: Who are the helpers in our school community?
How can we be a good neighbor?
misconceptions: Family means only a mom and a dad.
A neighbor is any friend, even one who lives far away.
A library is a place where you buy books.
extend: Make a class community map with a school, library, park, and homes, and label them together.
Invite a school helper, such as the librarian or custodian, to tell what they do.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit safe, share, together, and listen by asking how a community stays safe and shares space. Use community and helper again in unit 10 when children care for a class plant together, and library in unit 11 for books.

frames: A helper in my community is a ___.
wida.oral: Partner A names a helper without saying the job, such as 'I help you find books.' Partner B guesses the helper and says, 'You are a librarian.'

needsReview: Spanish glosses (familia, vecino, comunidad, ayudante, biblioteca) have not been reviewed by a native speaker; biblioteca is not the same as librería (bookstore) and may need a note.
Sense boundary: community is taught as the people who live and work in one place; the broader sense (a group with something in common) is left for grade 1 and later.
Sense boundary: family is taught as the people who care for each other at home; the animal family example in ex2 is a supporting use, not a second sense.
Morphology: helper (help + -er) is previewed in the study task only; no morph record is given because the unit is not a morphology unit.
